chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara who said:

I heard him say: There is no harm in marrying a Jewish or Christian woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah) even if he already has a permanent wife. As for what has been narrated in the reports that include rulings regarding what is established upon the validity of the contract, such as inheritance, divorce, and the waiting period (iddah), and similar matters, these reports encompass all that we have mentioned. It is also possible that these rulings are specific to a man who was Jewish or Christian and had a Jewish or Christian wife, and then he converted to Islam; for the contract does not cease upon his conversion, but remains valid, and these rulings apply to him according to what has come in the reports. And that which clarifies what we have mentioned.
ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on temporary marriage with Jewish or Christian women and how does conversion affect the marriage contract?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahani’s chain, Zurara clarifies that a Muslim man may marry a Jewish or Christian woman in mut'ah even while having a permanent wife, addressing the apparent tension with the general prohibition of marrying polytheists. The text further elucidates that legal rulings such as inheritance and iddah are context-dependent, potentially applying specifically to cases where a non-Muslim man converts to Islam while married to a non-Muslim woman, thereby preserving the validity of the existing contract. This highlights the Shia scholarly approach to reconciling specific textual evidence with broader jurisprudential principles.
